sources.title: Emergent Symmetries in Ensemble Averages

evidence.text: Roelcke–Selberg decomposition organizes the weighted difference between theta functions and their Eisenstein averages into cusp forms, Eisenstein residues, and continuous spectrum. The review associates these moduli-dependent corrections with symmetry breaking; a tower-of-states interpretation is only suggested.

sources.title: Emergent Symmetries in Ensemble Averages

evidence.text: Choi doubling and Schwinger–Keldysh generating functionals formulate mixed-state symmetries. Group twirling and Hubbard–Stratonovich auxiliary fields express weak-symmetry restoration through averages; the auxiliary weight is a quasi-probability distribution.

sources.title: Emergent Symmetries in Ensemble Averages

evidence.text: The reviewed Siegel–Weil proof compares modular cusp asymptotics and a shared differential equation, then invokes uniqueness through absence of a square-normalizable Laplacian eigenfunction with the required eigenvalue. It avoids explicit moduli integration.

evidence.text: The authors match the shell’s extrinsic-curvature discontinuity to its dust stress tensor, with m=4πR²σ. Solving the junction equation gives M′=M+(q²−m²−2qQ)/(2R)−m√(fII(R)+v²), where fII=1−2M/R+Q²/R². This is the paper’s classical shell calculation.
